<!-- pr-reviewer: 3ba3e93c48bff0e558c7174f37818fb163158504 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: merges at the next cut).

### What looks good
- Pure wiring, as claimed: no icon added or changed, no asset, no snapshot PNG, no dependency, build.rs, scripts or `.github` change.
- Glyphs are painted at 16 px through the existing `glyph` path (`fit_to_exact_size(Vec2::splat(16.0))`, body-ink tint), and degrade to the text alone when the icon set is not loaded.
- Row and item labels are unchanged: the catalog row still labels `"{name}  Ø{d} {kind}"`, and each picker item is still `selectable_value(idx, i, name)`.
- Layering holds: `named_glyph` and `tool_combo` call the app-layer `model::find_by_name` / `model::tool_of`. That is the pattern `pages.rs` already uses (`tool_page` calls `find_by_name` per catalog row). The ui makes no raw Flecs calls; `World` is only passed through as a type.
- `pages.rs` (1758 lines) grows by one line only; `op_page.rs` stays at 397 lines. `tool_icons.rs` has 85 lines and a provenance line.
- Process: conventional subject, `Changelog:` line, `Refs #661` (partial slice, so not `Fixes`), decision file in `docs/decisions/`, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, and no process files touched, so `PROCESS_VERSION` needs no bump.

### Local results (trial merge with origin/main 7a5816cf, clean, no conflicts)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --no-run` | built |
| `tool_icon_wiring` + `op_icon_table` (by name) | 6 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 607 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `camcraft-ui --test boundary` / `--test theme_files` | 3 passed / 14 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| Reviewer's throwaway kittest probe (local only, not pushed) | see below |

**Does the glyph actually get painted?** The PR's two tests pin only the pure choice (`catalog_row_icon`, `picker_item_icon`); nothing in them paints. So I ran a throwaway kittest probe locally. It called `IconSet::load(&h.ctx)` and then read the texture ids in the frame's shapes:
- **Tool page catalog:** all 29 catalog rows painted their kind's glyph (29 glyph images for 29 rows), and every row label (`"{name}  Ø{d} …"`) is in the AccessKit tree.
- **Picker (`tool_combo`, popup opened):** I added one document tool per kind in the catalog, 13 kinds in all. Every item that is visible in the popup painted its kind's texture, and no glyph was painted for a name with no tool. Each item's AccessKit label is exactly the tool name. Items below the popup's scroll fold are culled by egui as usual. Running the list in reverse order covered the last three kinds, so all 13 kinds were seen painted.

So the wiring works. The test gap is real, but it does not block a wiring PR.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **The tests do not paint.** `every_catalog_row_wears_its_kind_glyph` and `every_picker_item_wears_its_kind_glyph` would still pass if the `glyph(...)` call were removed from `pages.rs:1029` or from `tool_combo`. The smallest real pin is a kittest that:
   - calls `IconSet::load(&h.ctx)` on a `ShellUi::blank()` harness;
   - sets `ui_target = UiTarget::Tool(String::new())` and runs a few steps;
   - asserts that each catalog kind's `set.texture(tool_icon(kind)).id()` shows up among the painted `Shape::Rect` brush or `Shape::Mesh` texture ids.

   The picker gets the same check: a harness that draws `tool_combo` over a world holding one catalog tool per kind, clicks the `ComboBox` role, and makes the same assertion. It is about 60 lines and runs in under 0.2 s. A good follow-up (P7).
2. **The `tool_of_kind` fixture doc is wrong** (`tests/tool_icon_wiring.rs:12-14`). It says "every field but the kind is a real, valid tool". That holds for EndMill, BallNose, BullNose and Bore. For Drill, Tap, Turning, Groove, Thread, Form, Taper, Probe and Torch, `AddTool` refuses the swapped tool, so it never reaches the world. That is harmless for the pure mapping, but the comment overclaims. A fixture that takes the catalog's first tool of each kind would be honest.
3. **Per-frame cost.** `tool_combo` runs `model::find_by_name` + `tool_of` for every item on every frame, but only while the popup is open. `find_by_name` scans every `Name` entity and does not stop at the first match (`app/src/model.rs:100-108`). So an open popup costs O(items × named entities) per frame. That is fine at today's sizes. If documents grow, resolve the kinds once per frame, or have `find_by_name` return on the first match.
4. **`tool_combo` copies `fields::combo_owned`.** It is a near copy that differs only in the glyph. The glyph sits outside the `selectable_value`, so a click on the glyph does not pick the item. That is cosmetic. A `combo_owned_with(…, prefix: impl Fn(&mut Ui, &str))` would keep one combo.
5. Not exercised: nobody has looked at it on screen (no GUI was launched), and no pixel snapshot covers these rows. That is per policy; the structural/kittest probe above stands in for it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
